missing_papers.title: On-Chip Error-triggered Learning of Multi-layer Memristive Spiking Neural Networks
missing_papers.authors: Melika Payvand, Mohammed E. Fouda, Fadi Kurdahi, Ahmed M. Eltawil, Emre O. Neftci
missing_papers.venue: IEEE Journal on Emerging and Selected Topics in Circuits and Systems (JETCAS)
missing_papers.claim: A local, gradient-based, error-triggered learning rule with online ternary weight updates trains multi-layer SNNs on memristive crossbar hardware with only a small accuracy loss. The design shares crossbar and peripheral circuits between inference and training (subthreshold, 180 nm). The precursor paper (arXiv:1910.06152, 'Error-triggered Three-Factor Learning Dynamics for Crossbar Arrays') reports that error-triggering cuts the number of weight updates about 100-fold versus the standard rule at on-par accuracy (SPICE plus large-scale simulation, including gesture recognition).
missing_papers.why: This pre-empts the analog family's 'best honest-positive bet': a local rule on crossbars that needs far fewer device writes per accuracy has already been published, with about 100x fewer writes from event/error gating. Any C2 or write-budget study needs an error-triggered (thresholded) local-rule baseline, and can claim novelty only for the extra write savings from structure (pruning or hub budgets) on top of it.

missing_papers.title: Equivalent-accuracy accelerated neural-network training using analogue memory
missing_papers.authors: Stefano Ambrogio, Pritish Narayanan, Hsinyu Tsai, Robert M. Shelby, Irem Boybat, Carmelo di Nolfo, Severin Sidler, Massimo Giordano, et al. (14 authors per Crossref)
missing_papers.claim: In-situ backprop training on mixed hardware-software implementations of up to 204,900 synapses reached generalization accuracy equivalent to software on MNIST, MNIST-backrand, CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100. Each synapse combines long-term phase-change memory (PCM) storage with a near-linear volatile capacitor, plus 'polarity inversion' to cancel device-to-device variation. The calculated energy efficiency (28,065 GOP/s/W) and throughput per area (3.6 TOP/s/mm^2) exceed those of contemporary GPUs by about two orders of magnitude.
missing_papers.why: This directly contradicts the premise that backprop only 'plays at home' on GPUs. On an analog in-memory substrate, BP with a two-timescale (mixed-precision) synapse keeps software accuracy and is projected to be about 100x more efficient than a GPU. So the AIMC scoreboard's BP baseline must be analog BP of this kind (or Tiki-Taka/c-TTv2), not digital BP. The efficiency figure is a calculation, not a measurement.

missing_papers.title: Online Training of Spiking Recurrent Neural Networks with Phase-Change Memory Synapses
missing_papers.authors: Yigit Demirag, Charlotte Frenkel, Melika Payvand, Giacomo Indiveri
missing_papers.claim: Builds a simulation framework for differential-architecture crossbars based on a comprehensive PCM device model and trains a spiking RNN inside it with the local e-prop rule. Implementing the local e-prop updates directly on PCM is hard because of the devices' non-idealities. Of several widely used update schemes compared, gradient accumulation is what enables online, efficient training.
missing_papers.why: This is the closest precedent for how C2 is designed: a local rule running inside a device-model crossbar simulator, with update schemes compared. It implies that local rules also need digital gradient accumulation on realistic devices, which weakens the 'no data movement' argument. C2 should run NP/DFA both with and without accumulation (and with a Tiki-Taka-style transfer) and charge the accumulator's memory and energy.

missing_papers.title: L2ight: Enabling On-Chip Learning for Optical Neural Networks via Efficient in-situ Subspace Optimization
missing_papers.authors: Jiaqi Gu, Hanqing Zhu, Chenghao Feng, Zixuan Jiang, Ray T. Chen, David Z. Pan
missing_papers.venue: NeurIPS 2021 (per the official repository's citation block)
missing_papers.claim: In software simulation with photonic non-idealities, the zeroth-order on-chip protocols FLOPS and MixedTrain handle only toy ONNs of about 2,000 parameters. L2ight (calibration, then mapping of a pretrained model, then in-situ first-order subspace learning with multi-level sparsity) scales more than 1,000x further, to 10M parameters on CIFAR-100/ResNet-18. Where MixedTrain matches its accuracy, L2ight is still 1.7x faster and 6.9x more energy-efficient, using photonic tensor core (PTC) calls as a normalized energy proxy.
missing_papers.why: Strong counter-evidence: perturbative/zeroth-order learning loses badly even on a physical substrate where it is the 'natural' in-situ method. The winning recipe reuses a pretrained model and a gradient-based subspace update. C2's chances shrink unless it is scoped to small or adaptation layers. The paper also shows that sparsity inside on-chip training has already been explored.

missing_papers.title: On-Device Fine-Tuning via Backprop-Free Zeroth-Order Optimization
missing_papers.authors: Prabodh Katti, Houssem Sifaou, Sangwoo Park, Bipin Rajendran, Osvaldo Simeone
missing_papers.claim: Gives a theoretical estimate of the relative model sizes that fit in on-device memory under BP (stored activations and optimizer state, only partly relieved by checkpointing) versus memory-efficient zeroth-order optimization (MeZO, forward passes only). It then shows numerically that MeZO has accuracy advantages for on-device fine-tuning under memory constraints, provided enough wall-clock time is available.
missing_papers.why: This counters the project's equal-memory GPU result, where memory-saving BP beat forward gradient and NP: the opposite conclusion is published for the fine-tuning regime. It suggests the honest positive result for perturbative learners lies in adapting a pretrained network (low effective dimension), not in from-scratch class-incremental training. Any 'BP wins at equal memory' claim therefore needs a scope. The same group's arXiv:2608.21223 (implicit-perturbation zeroth-order training on IMC, 16 nm energy model, 0.46-0.83x the perturbation energy of explicit weight perturbation) appears in the tool notes but is missing from the paper table.

missing_papers.title: Loihi: A Neuromorphic Manycore Processor with On-Chip Learning
missing_papers.authors: Mike Davies, Narayan Srinivasa, Tsung-Han Lin, Gautham Chinya, Yongqiang Cao, Sri Harsha Choday, Georgios Dimou, Prasad Joshi, et al. (23 authors per Crossref)
missing_papers.claim: Loihi (60 mm^2, Intel 14 nm) integrates programmable synaptic learning rules on chip; its LASSO solver beats CPU solvers by over three orders of magnitude in energy-delay product. Later papers cite it for Loihi's learning cost of 120 pJ per synaptic update, taking 6.1 ns (Communications Engineering 2023, doi:10.1038/s44172-023-00117-9, ref. 51). A 2023 memristor learning engine reports 10.61 pJ per STDP update as 11.31x below Loihi (doi:10.1109/tbcas.2023.3291021), which is consistent with about 120 pJ. The paper itself is closed access and was not read; the number comes from these two secondary citations.
missing_papers.why: This fills a gap the neuromorphic scout named: no public per-update energy, so any per-update cost would have to be assumed. A C4 scoreboard built on the SANA-FE Loihi preset can use the published figure of about 120 pJ per synaptic update, a design figure rather than a measurement, instead of an undeclared assumption. It is also the seminal on-chip-learning chip paper a reviewer will expect; the list has only the 2021 Loihi survey.

missing_papers.title: Activity dependent structural plasticity in neuromorphic systems
missing_papers.authors: Richard George, Giacomo Indiveri, Stefano Vassanelli
missing_papers.venue: IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS) 2017
missing_papers.claim: In neuromorphic analog VLSI the number of synapse circuits is the binding limit on scalability. The paper proposes a runtime structural-plasticity mechanism that allocates this limited synapse pool, using neuronal activity to pick the event sources that best drive each postsynaptic neuron, so as to make optimal use of the on-chip resources.
missing_papers.why: This predates C4's core idea of activity-dependent allocation of a fixed synapse budget on a neuromorphic chip; the neuromorphic scout reported no hardware precedent. C4's novelty has to narrow to activity-proportional per-neuron budgets (hub allocation), combined with a class-incremental stream and NeuroBench-style costs.

missing_papers.title: A Simple Rule for Dendritic Spine and Axonal Bouton Formation Can Account for Cortical Reorganization after Focal Retinal Lesions
missing_papers.claim: Homeostatic structural plasticity: a neuron creates new spines and boutons when its electrical activity is below a homeostatic set point and removes them when its activity exceeds that set point. Spine and bouton formation depends only on the neuron's own activity. This rule reproduces cortical reorganization after focal retinal lesions. The neuromorphic tool notes say NEST's homeostatic structural plasticity follows this model.
missing_papers.why: The standard brain-derived rule for per-neuron connection budgets runs in the opposite direction to hub allocation, which gives budgets proportional to activity: here over-active neurons lose inputs. A reviewer will ask in what sense hub allocation is 'brain-like'. C1 and C4 should include the homeostatic (inverse-activity) budget as a control and justify the sign.

missing_papers.title: Analog Physical Systems Can Exhibit Double Descent
missing_papers.authors: Sam Dillavou, Jason W. Rocks, Jacob F. Wycoff, Andrea J. Liu, Douglas J. Durian
missing_papers.claim: Demonstrates double descent in a decentralized analog network of self-adjusting resistive elements that trains itself and runs tasks without a digital processor. Standard training fails to show double descent because of component non-idealities; a modified protocol that accommodates the imperfection succeeds. The authors argue that physical (and perhaps biological) learners benefit from over-parameterization.
missing_papers.why: This is counter-evidence for C3's subtractive premise. In the very substrate C3 targets, adding edges improves generalization, so removing edges during learning can land on the interpolation peak. C3 must report test accuracy against edge count along the whole double-descent curve, not only power and training fit.

missing_papers.title: Frequency Propagation: Multimechanism Learning in Nonlinear Physical Networks
missing_papers.authors: Vidyesh Rao Anisetti, Ananth Kandala, Benjamin Scellier, J. M. Schwarz
missing_papers.claim: In a nonlinear resistive network with variable resistors, an activation current is applied at the input nodes at one frequency and an error current at the output nodes at another, at the same time. Each conductance is updated in proportion to the product of the two frequency-demodulated local coefficients. The rule is local and proven to perform gradient descent, and the paper frames it as 'multi-mechanism learning' that covers electrical, elastic and flow networks.
missing_papers.why: This is the closest precedent found for C5: inference and error signals coexist in one physical network, with no separate free and nudged phases. It can be implemented directly in the resistor-network simulator recommended for C3. C5's novelty therefore reduces to the pruning component, and frequency propagation belongs next to EP and coupled learning as a baseline.

missing_papers.title: Self-learning Machines based on Hamiltonian Echo Backpropagation
missing_papers.claim: Gives a general scheme for autonomous self-learning in any time-reversible Hamiltonian system: the parameter updates happen autonomously, with no external processing and no need to know or control the internal parameters. It is demonstrated numerically on coupled nonlinear wave fields. A 2025 follow-up (arXiv:2506.06248) derives Hamiltonian Echo Learning as a special case of Lagrangian EP and notes that it is forward-only, local, and needs only two or more passes through the system regardless of model size.
missing_papers.why: This counters the view that local rules win on physical substrates while backprop belongs to GPUs: gradient learning can itself be native to physics. A physical-substrate scoreboard for C3 and C5 should include physical BP-like methods as baselines (Hamiltonian echo methods, in-situ photonic BP), not only digital BP.

missing_papers.title: Training Deep Boltzmann Networks with Sparse Ising Machines
missing_papers.authors: Shaila Niazi, Navid Anjum Aadit, Masoud Mohseni, Shuvro Chowdhury, Yao Qin, Kerem Y. Camsari
missing_papers.claim: Sparse, asynchronous, massively parallel p-bit Ising machines on FPGAs train deep Boltzmann networks in a hybrid probabilistic-classical loop. They use full MNIST and Fashion-MNIST and a reduced CIFAR-10, with hardware-aware sparse topologies. On MNIST, about 30,000 parameters (4,264 p-bits) match the 90% accuracy of a software RBM with about 3.25M parameters, and only the sparse network can also generate digits. The machine runs a measured 50-64 billion flips/s, at least an order of magnitude faster than GPU/TPU implementations, and handles CD-n with up to 10 million sweeps per update.
missing_papers.why: Probabilistic computers are a non-von-Neumann family no scout searched. A local contrastive rule and hardware-imposed sparsity are native there, and a sparse network matching a roughly 100x larger dense model is already shown, which makes it a candidate venue for hub-style sparse topologies. Caveats: weight updates are computed classically, and 90% on MNIST is low.

missing_angles: Learning regime: perturbative learners were judged only on from-scratch training. Published evidence says zeroth-order or perturbative learning wins under device-memory limits mainly when it adapts a pretrained model (Katti 2025, arXiv:2511.11362; MeZO, arXiv:2305.17333). Untested: NP or ZO adaptation of a last layer or LoRA-style branch on an AIMC simulator while the backbone stays frozen in analog arrays (compare arXiv:2601.10037: hybrid analog-digital LoRA mapping that cuts the analog training/update cost by up to 148x). Lei et al. 2026 (arXiv:2608.21223) should move from the tool notes into the paper table.

1990s analog-VLSI perturbative learning is absent, and a reviewer will expect it for C2. Weight perturbation for analog VLSI: Jabri & Flower, Neural Computation 1991 (doi:10.1162/neco.1991.3.4.546) and IEEE TNN 1992 (doi:10.1109/72.105429). Cauwenberghs' analog VLSI recurrent network that learns a trajectory (IEEE TNN 1996, doi:10.1109/72.485671). Maeda's simultaneous-perturbation analog and FPGA circuits (doi:10.1109/ijcnn.1993.714047; doi:10.1109/tnn.2003.811357). Hirotsu & Brooke's random-weight-change chip (doi:10.1109/ijcnn.1993.714359). Memristor versions exist at toy scale: weight simultaneous perturbation (Nonlinear Dynamics 2019, doi:10.1007/s11071-018-4730-z) and a node-perturbation-like 'weighted-sum simultaneous perturbation' run fully on a PSpice memristor circuit (odd parity; a 16-10-6 face recognition net; Neurocomputing 2021, doi:10.1016/j.neucom.2021.08.072). C2's novelty must therefore be scale, a calibrated device model, a head-to-head against Tiki-Taka, and cost accounting, not 'perturbation on memristors' as such.

In-materio substrates (dopant-network processing units, DNPUs) were not searched. Homodyne gradient extraction perturbs every parameter with its own sinusoid and reads gradients by lock-in detection directly in the material (Nature Communications 2025, doi:10.1038/s41467-025-65155-7; arXiv:2105.11233). DNPU classification: Nature 2020, doi:10.1038/s41586-019-1901-0. These are close cousins of MGD and Lock-in EP, which are already in the list.

C1 prior art on crossbar-structured pruning is missing from the table. Crossbar-grain and column-grain sparsity cut crossbar overhead by 44-72% on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet (Liang et al., IEEE Access 2018, arXiv:1807.10816). Group Scissor's group connection deletion cuts the routing area between crossbars (DAC 2017, arXiv:1702.03443, doi:10.1145/3061639.3062256). TinyADC prunes so that ADCs need fewer bits, with 3.5x lower power and 2.9x smaller area (DATE 2021, doi:10.23919/date51398.2021.9474235). For hub allocation itself, the closest ML relative was not searched: OWL (arXiv:2310.05175) sets each layer's sparsity in proportion to its activation-outlier ratio and beats Wanda at 70% sparsity. A reviewer will compare per-neuron hub budgets with OWL.

Concurrent and asynchronous learning in physical networks goes beyond frequency propagation. Desynchronous, clock-free per-edge updates do not hurt learning, and in experiment they help (Wycoff et al., J. Chem. Phys. 2022, arXiv:2201.04626, doi:10.1063/5.0084631). Temporal Contrastive Learning uses integral feedback as an implicit memory and derives a Landauer-like energy cost of learning, a physical lower bound usable for C3/C5 scoring (Nature Communications 2025, arXiv:2312.17723, doi:10.1038/s41467-025-57043-x). Perturbative Contrastive Physical Learning (arXiv:2606.09756) unifies these contrast-based schemes in spring networks and continuous-variable photonics.

Pruning risk for physical learners: in linear circuits, EP, coupled learning and adjoint coupled learning converge exponentially only under a coercivity (rank) condition on a matrix built from the network's incidence structure (arXiv:2606.15443). Removing edges changes that structure, so C3 should check the condition as it prunes.

Device-level metaplasticity as the substrate's own answer to class-incremental forgetting, in place of replay buffers, was not searched. Metaplastic binarized networks: Nature Communications 2021, doi:10.1038/s41467-021-22768-y. Metaplasticity on multi-level RRAM: a fabricated 130 nm array learned MNIST then Fashion-MNIST at 97% and 86%, equal to software, and is endurance-compatible (arXiv:2306.12142). A Benna-Fusi complex synapse realized with proton transistors (arXiv:2401.15045).

Measured silicon that learns while inferring is under-listed in the neuromorphic family. ReckOn (ISSCC 2022, arXiv:2208.09759, doi:10.1109/ISSCC42614.2022.9731734) learns online with e-prop at under 150 uW training power and 0.8% memory overhead. EqSpike (iScience 2021, doi:10.1016/j.isci.2021.102222) gives model-based estimates that spiking EP in silicon would use 2-3 orders of magnitude less energy than GPUs. The lifelong-learning accelerator design principles paper (Kudithipudi et al., arXiv:2310.04467) should frame the C4/C5 metrics.

Tools missing from the tool lists. EBANA is an open-source, Keras-like framework that generates SPICE-level analog circuits and trains them with EP (Frontiers in Computational Neuroscience 2023, doi:10.3389/fncom.2023.1114651); it gives circuit-level power for C3 without hand-written SPICE. A physics-derived valence-change-memory (VCM) memristor model integrated into aihwkit (arXiv:2403.06746) covers device dynamics that lookup tables miss.

Update disturbance: fully parallel in-array weight updates disturb neighbouring cross-point devices (arXiv:2608.25781, Advanced Science 2026). This is my inference: pruned devices held at minimum conductance may still be disturbed, so 'a pruned device is never written' overstates the savings, and the C1/C2 write accounting should model disturbance.

Perturbation theory relevant to the NP divergence and to choosing NP or WP on crossbars. Weight perturbation often matches or beats node perturbation on temporally extended, low-dimensional tasks (Zuge et al., PRX 2023, doi:10.1103/physrevx.13.021006). Hiratani et al., 'On the Stability and Scalability of Node Perturbation Learning' (NeurIPS 2022, doi:10.52202/068431-2314) was verified by title only; its abstract was not readable.

Correction to the existing list: 'Reconfigurable Digital RRAM Logic Enables In-Situ Pruning and Learning for Edge AI' is arXiv:2506.13151, by Songqi Wang, Yue Zhang, Jia Chen and 10 others (13 authors; Zhongrui Wang is 11th), not Zhongrui Wang alone. It prunes during training by weight similarity on a fabricated 180 nm digital 1T1R RRAM CIM chip (MNIST 91.44%, ModelNet10 77.75%) and reports energy compared with analog RRAM CIM and with an RTX 4090.
